incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high p95 token latency + stream stalls on /v1/chat/stream detected for region us-west-2. Severity: P2. Paging Alex (on-call)

Alex (on-call): I’m on it. seeing a spike in stream connection backlog and GPU KV evictions in dashboards. p95 token latency ~1.8s -> 3.9s over last 12m.

Mica (SRE): Confirmed. Redisish cache churn and RT throttles. A bunch of streaming connections are sitting waiting for KV updates, causing head-of-line. Throughput drops for non-stream as well.

Priya (eng-runtime): Likely root cause: continuous-batching + streaming interop bug on recent kernel selection change. Streaming paths holding onto per-request state longer than expected. I can roll a quick mitigation: temporarily disable streaming responses for affected routes.

Alex (on-call): That matches what I saw. Customers hitting streaming endpoints see spiky latency and 429s after queue fills. We should mitigate traffic before a broader degradation. Options: 1) global streaming toggle off, 2) rate-limit streaming endpoints, 3) route streaming to lower-capacity pool.

Sam (product): Customer impact? Which customers are on streaming by default? Luke can coordinate comms.

Luke (CS): A few PLG customers have streaming enabled by default; our largest affected users are org-67 and org-92 (internal tags). If we flip streaming off they’ll get non-streamed responses (slower start-of-response) but more reliable. We should warn them.

Mica (SRE): Proposed immediate plan: A) flip feature-flag to disable streaming globally for hosted API in us-west-2 (canary first). B) apply emergency rate limits (20 rps per org for streaming endpoints) while we verify. C) monitor p95/p99 and KV eviction rate.

Priya (eng-runtime): I can push the flag. Command (internal FF service):

```
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/v1/flags/streaming_off \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"environments":{"us-west-2":"on"},"actor":"incident"}'
```

Priya (eng-runtime): Will do a canary on pool-a (10% traffic) first, then 100% if metrics improve.

Alex (on-call): Execute canary now. Start with pool-a. I’ll watch traces and request queue length.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated: feature-flag/streaming_off -> pool-a (canary, 10%) by Priya.

Priya (eng-runtime): Canary flipped at 1758009940.

Mica (SRE): Seeing initial signals: streaming connection backlog down 35% in pool-a. KV eviction delta falling. p95 tokens down to ~1.6s.

Alex (on-call): Good. Proceed to 100% in us-west-2. Priya, apply global toggle and attach temporary rate-limit rule: streaming endpoints -> 20 rps/org for 30m. Config snippet: 

```
rlctl set --endpoint /v1/chat/stream --region us-west-2 --limit 20 --window 1m --scope org
```

Priya (eng-runtime): Global toggle set at 1758010045. Rate limit rule applied at 1758010070.

Mica (SRE): Metrics after global: p95 tokens down to 0.9s, queue depth normalized, error rate dropped from 6% -> 0.7%. GPU utilization stabilizing.

Alex (on-call): Nice. Customer perf improved. Luke: please draft a short comms to affected customers: we disabled streaming temporarily to stabilize latency, responses will fall back to non-stream mode. We'll restore streaming after patch.

Luke (CS): On it. Draft: "We temporarily disabled streaming in us-west-2 due to increased latency; you will receive full responses instead of streaming. We're working on a fix and will update in 1-2 hours." Want to send now?

Sam (product): Wait — can we estimate rollback time? Engineering?

Priya (eng-runtime): Need ~90m for a targeted runtime fix and a safe canary. I recommend keeping streaming disabled until fix shipped and validated. We can extend rate limits/controls if customers need more time.

Mica (SRE): Also enabling traffic shaping at the edge to prioritize non-streaming low-latency requests. edge-config change: set streaming route weight 0 for us-west-2.

Alex (on-call): Handing off the incident to Mica for stabilization and patch rollout. I’ll update the incident channel and rotate out after next hour.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3452 | High p95 latency + streaming stalls | assigned: Mica (SRE), priority P2 | started 1758009876

Mica (SRE): Handoff notes: watch p95 tokens, KV eviction metric, and 429 climb. Correlate with pool routing. I’ll coordinate with Priya on the patch and with Luke for customer updates.

Priya (eng-runtime): Patch branch created: fix/streaming-kv-hold. Will run unit + canary tests. Plan: land patch, build, deploy to pool-a, validate 15m, then roll to rest.

Mica (SRE): Post-mitigation checklist: 1) confirm error rate <1% for 20m. 2) rollback streaming toggle only after patch validated. 3) remove temporary rate limits and edge weight. 4) update status page.

Luke (CS): Sent comms to affected customers at 1758010450. Message included reason, ETA, and support contact.

Alex (on-call): I’m going to rest. Mica you’ve got the pager. If anything regresses, escalate to oncall rotation and tag Sam.

Sam (product): Thx. Also note for postmortem: decide whether streaming should be opt-in vs default for new orgs.

Priya (eng-runtime): Canary build started at 1758011500. Will post logs and test results here.

Mica (SRE): Keeping monitoring alarms enabled. Setting temporary dashboard annotation: "streaming disabled - emergency".

incident-bot: Update: incident INC-2026-3452 severity remains P2. Next update expected in 30m.

Priya (eng-runtime): Early canary looks good. No regressions in non-stream path. Preparing rollout plan for full fix deploy once tests finish.

Mica (SRE): Thanks team. Saving timeline: initial page 1758009876, canary toggle 1758009940, global toggle 1758010045, rate limits 1758010070, customer comms 1758010450.

Luke (CS): Will follow up with customers after fix is verified.

Sam (product): Add follow-up action: evaluate streaming toggle as circuit-breaker in the console for future incidents.

Alex (on-call): Back on rotation but reachable if needed. Good job everyone. :white_check_mark:
